Bank reconciliation

Proves your bank statement and your books differ only for reasons you can name (timing, fees, bounced items) and finds what is left over.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, Operating account (…4471), September. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin bank reconciliation skill

Can you reconcile our operating account for September?

Claude

Yes. Before I read anything, I need six answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
  2. Which account? I show account numbers masked.
  3. Which period? I never assume one.
  4. Please attach the bank statement.
  5. When did you last reconcile this account?
  6. What size of difference is worth chasing?

Use MosoFin. Operating account ending 4471, September. Statement attached. We reconciled August. Chase anything over $10.

📄 operating-4471-september.pdf
MosoFinChecked the workspace and the company fileread-only✓
  1. WorkspaceNorthbrook Trading
  2. Company fileConfirmed by name
  3. ToolsRead-only tools only

The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

Claude

Here is my plan for Operating (…4471), 1 to 30 September. I will read the books, agree the opening balance, match every statement line and propose entries for what is left. Shall I start?

Yes, go ahead.

MosoFinRead the books in one batchread-only✓
  1. search_accountsOperating (…4471)
  2. get_trial_balanceRead
  3. get_general_ledgerBook balance $12,155.50
  4. search_depositsIncludes $1,250.00 banked 30 Sep
  5. search_bill_paymentsIncludes #1031 to Acme Supplies
  6. search_purchasesRead
  7. search_paymentsRead
  8. search_transfersRead
  9. search_journal_entriesRead

9 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

Claude

The statement ends at $12,480.00. Two items explain the bank side, and both are timing:

Bank side
Statement ending balance$12,480.00
+ Deposit in transit, banked 30 Sep$1,250.00
− Cheque #1043, not yet cashed$1,860.00
= Adjusted bank balance$11,870.00

Nothing in the books needs to change for these two items.

Claude

Your books say $12,155.50. Three statement lines are not in the books, and one payment is in the books twice:

Book side
Book balance$12,155.50
− Bank fee, statement line 14 Sep$15.00
+ Interest, statement line 30 Sep$4.50
− Customer cheque returned, statement line 19 Sep$300.00
+ Duplicate payment #1031 reversed$25.00
= Adjusted book balance$11,870.00
Difference to the adjusted bank balance$0.00

Cheque #1031 to Acme Supplies is in the books twice, with the same date, amount and reference.

Claude

I propose four entries. Each one points to its evidence:

Proposed entries
EntryAmountEvidence
Record the bank fee$15.00Statement line, 14 Sep
Record the interest$4.50Statement line, 30 Sep
Reverse the returned cheque to what the customer owes$300.00Statement line, 19 Sep
Reverse the duplicate payment #1031$25.00The two book entries

The $300 goes back to what the customer owes. It is not an expense. Please also chase the customer.

Claude

The reconciliation ties to the cent. Your report has the summary, the matched and open items, the exceptions, the proposed entries and the coverage.
